Arabic vowel-less forms (e.g. 'معرّض') are ambiguous. Whether the app displays diacritics affects the severity of that finding.
summary: I checked all 1210 lemma-language pairs (121 lemmas × 10 languages) and flagged 37 findings: 1 high, 22 medium and 14 low. Recurring issues: 'confusion' glossed as mental bewilderment instead of commotion (6 languages); 'wardrobe' glossed only as furniture when the context means a clothes collection (8 languages, likely inherited from the reference); and 'find' glossed as 'search' in hi and ur. Other notable cases are 'have' as 'keep/place' (hi, ur), 'short' as 'brief' (ur), 'remained' as 'stayed' (vi), and an ambiguous passive reading of Arabic 'endangering'. Most other glosses look acceptable for their context. Findings marked 'requires-native-review' need native confirmation, and this sample does not establish that the full glossary is correct.
